Rachel —

Thanks for the quick intro call yesterday. Procurement timeline: we want vendor responses by EOD Friday so the SRE architecture review can happen next week.

Samuel Park

From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>

Samuel / Maya —

Appreciate the clear ask. I've attached an initial capacity_headroom_matrix_v1.xlsx and a short load_test_plan.md that covers our standard methodology. High level notes up front: 

- The matrix shows recommended QPS targets for our hosted "Prod" tier and for a Dedicated baseline with 8 GPUs and with a 16-GPU burst profile. Each row lists expected median token/sec, P95 token latency (ms), and session concurrency to match your prompt-length distribution.
- Key assumptions: 16k sequence max, KV-cache enabled for multi-turn sessions, steady-state prefix reuse of ~40% for your conversational mix. Cold-starts are modeled separately in the last tab.
- Test harness: we use a replay + jitter generator that replays recorded session traces and injects Poisson arrival noise; each run is 30m with a 10m warmup. Tail (P99.9) is sampled across replicas and includes queuing time.

Questions for you that will adjust the numbers: 
- Do you expect long multi-turn sessions to hold a single session ID pinned to one replica (sticky routing) or do you plan stateless fallback?
- What SLAs do you require for failover to an alternate region (if any)?

I'll loop in our SRE and performance team to validate edge cases; expect a follow-up with refined numbers and the test-run artifacts by tomorrow EOD.

Best,
Rachel Kim
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
rachel_kim@redwood.com

Rachel / Kim —

Quick validation and recommendations: 

- P99.9 guidance: provide cluster-level P99.9 with an annotation explaining that per-replica P99.9 is highly sensitive to request routing and queue discipline; cluster-level better reflects user experience for a multi-replica endpoint.
- Tail sampling window: we sample P99.9 across 1-hour sliding windows over the 30m steady-state run and report median of windows across 3 runs (so the number is resilient to transient noise). Include the raw run artifacts for transparency.
- Batching: assumptions in the sheet use adaptive micro-batching with a 50ms max delay and dynamic batch sizing capped by model context tokens. For their median 120-token prompt, batching yield is modest; for longer prompts we model lower batch efficiency.
- KV-cache: we modeled 40% prefix reuse for the "conversation" profile; if Altitude expects session stickiness (single replica), add a column for optimistic reuse 70% (lower cost).
- Dedicated sizing: the 8-GPU option assumes A100-equivalent hardware with 32-bit mixed precision; the 16-GPU burst line is for traffic lifecycle events and assumes autoscaling within 3 minutes to full burst.

I'll prepare a short paragraph for each bullet that they can paste into their architecture review. Also adding a short note on how we measure cold-start contribution (measured separately by forcing a replica restart and measuring first 5 requests).

Karthik
